story_type: one unbroken tracking shot of a moon rocket from liftoff through the sound barrier to first stage separation
hook: One camera never let go of Apollo 11.
narration: One camera followed Apollo 11 from the pad until its first stage fell away.
It was a cinetheodolite, a tracking camera that also records exactly where it points, so engineers could plot the flight.
On July sixteenth, 1969, it watched five engines lift the rocket off the pad.
Then a cloud wrapped itself around the rocket.
That was air condensing in the shock waves as the Saturn V pushed through the speed of sound.
Higher up, in thinner air, the flame spread wider and wider.
Soon it was a burning point, high over the Atlantic.
outcome: Its first stage fell away soon after, and Apollo 11 climbed on toward orbit with its three astronauts.
title: Apollo 11 tracked in one unbroken shot
description:
On July 16, 1969, a NASA cinetheodolite tracking camera followed the Apollo 11 Saturn V in a single sequence from liftoff to about a minute after first stage separation.

Footage: NASA Johnson Space Center film, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Flight_of_AS-506_(Apollo_11)_from_lift-off_to_1_min_after_S-IC_stage_separation,_VJSC_1425D-q1.ogv
